title: When no check works: quiet moves and "no forced mate"
outcomes: Searches in order: every check, then captures next to the king, then quiet moves that threaten mate
Counts the enemy king's legal moves before and after a quiet move
Rejects a quiet move that allows a counter-check or meets an extra defender on the mating square
Answers "no forced mate in two" and names what stops the candidate

steps.text: When no check works, look for a **quiet move**: not a check, but a threat of mate that no reply can meet. Search in this order: every check, then captures next to the king, then quiet moves. For a quiet move ask: how many moves does the king have? Can the defender check, or take my attacking piece? Does every reply allow mate? This order is a *rule of thumb*: it saves time and proves nothing.

steps.caption: White to move. The only check is Nc7+. Test it, then look for a quiet move.

line.say: A quiet move. The black king has no legal move, and Nc7 would be mate.
Black has to move something else.

claims.statement: After the check Nc7+ the black king still has two legal moves, so it is not mate.
Nc7+ is far worse than Ka6 (at least ten pawns, depth 16).
After Ka6 the black king has no legal move.

steps.text: **Two ways a quiet move fails.** First, a counter-check: the defender gives check, a check must be answered at once, and the mate never comes. Second, one extra defender covering the mating square. A threat of mate is not a mate: it counts only if every reply, every check included, still loses. *Rule of thumb:* after your quiet move, list the defender's checks and captures first.

steps.title: One more defender
steps.prompt: In the first position Nxd7 forces mate. Now one black pawn stands on a different square. Predict, then check.

steps.title: A counter-check
steps.prompt: In the first position Qh6 forces mate. Now one black rook has moved. Predict, then check.

steps.text: No labels now. In each position decide: is there a forced mate in two? If you think so, find the first move. If you think not, say so, and name what stops it. The next three exercises are silent.

steps.prompt: Which part of the search is least secure: counting the king's legal moves, listing the defender's checks, or deciding that there is no mate? In your next game, when you find a threat of mate, write down the defender's checks before you play it.
